'''Luca Gammaitoni''' (born 16 June 1961 in Perugia) is a scientist in the area of [[noise]] and [[nonlinear dynamics]]. He is currently the Director of the Noise in Physical System Laboratory (NiPS Lab) at the Physics Department of the [[Università di Perugia]], in Italy.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Luca Gammaitoni, Dipartimento di Fisica Perugia |url=http://www.fisica.unipg.it/~luca.gammaitoni/ |access-date=2023-10-01 |website=www.fisica.unipg.it}}</ref>

==Education and career==

He graduated in physics at the [[University of Perugia]] and obtained his Ph.D. in physics from the [[University of Pisa]] in 1991 (S. Santucci advisor) with a thesis entitled "[[Stochastic Resonance]]". He is currently Professor of Physics at the Faculty of Science of the [[University of Perugia]] in Italy and the Director of The Noise in Physical Systems (NiPS) Laboratory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NiPS Laboratory – Noise in Physical Systems |url=https://www.nipslab.org/ |access-date=2023-10-01 |language=en-US}}</ref> NiPS, a research facility within the Physics Department of the [[University of Perugia]], has a long-standing tradition in studying physical systems in the presence of noise. 

In 2004	he was awarded the First prize for innovation ideas, a Spin-off competition, of the [[University of Perugia]]. Eventually, this led to the establishment of Wisepower srl.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.wisepower.it/en/home/ | title=Home }}</ref> An innovative company devoted to the development of advanced technology in the field of self-powered wireless devices.

In 2016 he received the Special Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics for the observation of gravitational waves, opening new horizons in astronomy and physics,<ref>{{cite web | url=https://breakthroughprize.org/News/32 | title=Breakthrough Prize – Special Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics Awarded for Detection of Gravitational Waves 100 Years After Albert Einstein Predicted Their Existence }}</ref> as a member of the LIGO-Virgo collaboration.

In 2016-2019 he served as President of the Fondazione POST (Museo della Scienza di Perugia).<ref>https://www.perugiapost.it</ref>

During the Covid-19 pandemic, together with Igor Neri, proposed a stochastic model for dealing with fluctuations in epidemic diffusion.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Neri |first1=I. |last2=Gammaitoni |first2=L. |title=Role of fluctuations in epidemic resurgence after a lockdown |journal=Scientific Reports |date=19 March 2021 |volume=11 |issue=1 |page=6452 |doi=10.1038/s41598-021-85808-z  |doi-access=free|pmid=33742018 |pmc=7979713 |bibcode=2021NatSR..11.6452N }}{{psc|date=May 2024}}</ref>

His scientific papers received more than 100.000 citations.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=uZet4d0AAAAJ&hl=en | title=Luca Gammaitoni }}</ref>

==Scientific Interests==
* Stochastic nonlinear dynamics with specific reference to [[Stochastic Resonance]], [[dithering]], resonant trapping, resonant crossing phenomena.
* Noise limits in the operation of [[Gravitational Waves]] detectors<ref>{{Cite web |last=Neri |first=Igor |last2=López-Suárez |first2=Miquel |last3=Gammaitoni |first3=Luca |date=2017-06-10 |title=Operating Gravitational Wave Detectors far from equilibrium |url=https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.04067v2 |access-date=2026-07-27 |website=arXiv.org |language=en}}</ref>
* [[Energy Harvesting]], with specific reference to nonlinear vibration harvesting, micro and nanoscale energy management [https://web.archive.org/web/20170811181935id_/http://www.nipslab.org/sites/nipslab.org/files/PhysRevLett_102_080601_0.pdf]
* [[Efficient energy use|Energy efficiency]] in computing devices, with specific reference to micro and nanoscale logic gate devices {{ISBN|978-9535130116}}
* [[Thermal noise]] and non-equilibrium relaxation processes in solid state systems {{ISBN|978-1-4799-2069-3}}
* [[Thermodynamics]] of computing and fundamental limits in the physics of computation<ref>{{Cite journal |last=López-Suárez |first=M. |last2=Neri |first2=I. |last3=Gammaitoni |first3=L. |date=2016-06-28 |title=Sub-kBT micro-electromechanical irreversible logic gate |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/ncomms12068 |journal=Nature Communications |language=en |volume=7 |issue=1 |article-number=12068 |doi=10.1038/ncomms12068  |doi-access=free|issn=2041-1723|pmc=4931245 }}</ref>
* [[Epidemics]] spreading and the role of fluctuations<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Neri |first=I. |last2=Gammaitoni |first2=L. |date=2021-03-19 |title=Role of fluctuations in epidemic resurgence after a lockdown |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-021-85808-z |journal=Scientific Reports |language=en |volume=11 |issue=1 |page=6452 |doi=10.1038/s41598-021-85808-z  |doi-access=free|issn=2045-2322|pmc=7979713 }}</ref>
* [[Artificial Intelligence]] fundamental limits in Big Data and Machine Learning applications<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gammaitoni |first=Luca |date=2021-06-02 |title=Why it is difficult to find something, if you do not know what you are looking for |url=https://medium.com/geekculture/why-it-is-difficult-to-find-something-if-you-do-not-know-what-you-are-looking-for-1e7ca2f69da5 |access-date=2026-07-27 |website=Geek Culture |language=en}}</ref>
